text: {"batchcomplete":true,"query":{"pages":[{"pageid":42070652,"ns":0,"title":"Abnormal grain growth","extract":"In materials science, abnormal or discontinuous grain growth, also referred to as exaggerated or secondary recrystallisation grain growth, is a grain growth phenomenon in which certain energetically favorable grains (crystallites) grow rapidly in a matrix of finer grains, resulting in a bimodal distribution of grain size.\nIn ceramic materials, this phenomenon can result in the formation of elongated prismatic, acicular (needle-like) grains in a densified matrix.","description":"Phenomenon of certain material grains growing faster than others","descriptionsource":"local"}]}}
